neighbours.label: ' enough' after an adjective or adverb (good enough, long enough)
fire: The old laptop is still fast enough for writing emails and reports.
She decided the rough sketch was good enough to show the client.
Two hours in the oven was not long enough for the turkey to cook through.
The coach said our defence was strong enough to win the league.
Is the rope thick enough to hold a grown man's weight?
Their apology was sincere enough that the neighbours let it go.
The hall was big enough to seat every family in the village.
He wasn't old enough to drive, so his sister took him to practice.
quiet: The old laptop is still very fast for writing emails and reports.
She decided the rough sketch was too good to throw away before the meeting.
Two hours in the oven was far too long for the small chicken.
The coach said our defence was the strongest in the whole league.
Is the rope thicker than the one we used on the boat last week?
Their apology was so sincere that the neighbours let it go.
The hall was big and bright, with seats for every family in the village.
He was too young to drive, so his sister took him to practice.

notes: Card top 32: ' enough' x15; logit effect promotes sufficient/suffice/enough. Near misses keep the sentences with the bare adjective or a different degree word.
